tasks.title: Rate limit at MAV_n_RATE = 0
tasks.statement: A MAVLink instance is on a port at **{b}** baud, `MAV_n_RATE` = 0. What rate limit (bytes/s) does the firmware use?
tasks.solution: `mavlink_main.cpp`: with a zero limit `_datarate = _baudrate / 20`. On an 8N1 port a byte is 10 bits, so the port limit is `baud / 10`; the firmware takes half. This rule is for UART; on USB (`/dev/ttyACM*`) zero means 100 000 B/s.

tasks.title: MAVLink rate multiplier
tasks.statement: `MAV_0_RATE` = **{r}** B/s. Constant-rate streams (HEARTBEAT) take 21 B/s. By the sum of "size × rate" the scalable streams need **{s}** B/s. Find the `tx rate mult` multiplier (with the 0.05…1 bounds).
tasks.solution: `update_rate_mult()`: mult = (limit − constant-rate) / scalable, then constrained to 0.05…1. The multiplier never goes above 1, so rates do not rise beyond what is configured.

tasks.title: Actual message rate
tasks.statement: Port at **{b}** baud, `MAV_n_RATE` = 0. The scalable streams need **{s}** B/s, the constant-rate ones 21 B/s. A message is configured for **{f}** Hz. At what rate will it go out?
tasks.solution: Limit = baud / 20. mult = (limit − 21) / scalable sum, constrained to 0.05…1. Rate = configured × mult.

tasks.title: How many bytes per second a stream takes
tasks.statement: A MAVLink 2 message with a **{p}**-byte payload is sent at **{f}** Hz. How many bytes per second does the firmware budget for it when computing the multiplier?
tasks.solution: The stream size is the full payload length + 12 bytes (10 of header and 2 of checksum, no signature), times the rate: `MAVLINK_MSG_ID_*_LEN + MAVLINK_NUM_NON_PAYLOAD_BYTES`.

tasks.title: Receiver weight when blending two GPS units
tasks.statement: `SENS_GPS_MASK` = 2 (horizontal accuracy only). The first receiver reports `eph` = **{a}** m, the second **{c}** m, both have a 3D fix. What weight does the first receiver get?
tasks.solution: `gps_blending.cpp`: the weight is inversely proportional to the square of the error and normalized: w₁ = (1/eph₁²) / (1/eph₁² + 1/eph₂²) = eph₂² / (eph₁² + eph₂²). The more accurate receiver gets the larger weight; with equal eph both get 0.5.

tasks.title: GPS_1_GNSS mask
tasks.statement: You need to enable these systems on a u-blox: GPS (bit 0), Galileo (bit 2), plus bits **{x}** and **{y}** (1 SBAS, 3 BeiDou, 4 GLONASS, 5 NAVIC). What number goes into `GPS_1_GNSS`?
tasks.solution: Mask = sum of 2^bit: GPS 1 + Galileo 4 + 2^x + 2^y. For example, GPS + SBAS + Galileo + GLONASS = 1 + 2 + 4 + 16 = 23.
